moments.title: The Berkshire meeting that sparked an ETF
moments.insight: Sitting at Warren Buffett's first meeting without Charlie Munger, the founder feared what happens to Berkshire when Buffett dies.

moments.title: Why the S&P buys more of a stock as founders leave
moments.insight: Free-float adjusting means index funds buy MORE of a company after its owner-operator retires, sells, or dies—backwards from what investors should want.

moments.title: IBM's fall: proof leadership departure kills dominance
moments.insight: IBM was 2.5x larger than its nearest competitor in 1984, but fell out of the top 10 within eight years of its owner-chairman retiring.

moments.title: The 100-bagger secret: 19 of 21 shared one trait
moments.insight: Studying every stock that returned 100x since 2000, 19 of 21 had insider ownership above 5% before their massive run-up.

moments.title: Zoo lion vs. wild lion: the CEO metaphor
moments.insight: A hired 'zoo lion' CEO gets paid regardless of performance, while an owner-operator 'wild lion' feels the pain of mistakes directly.
